outcome: No developments found since 26 January 2024. The general form of Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points (that the closure of V(Q) in V(R) has finitely many connected components for any variety V over Q) was already disproven before the frozen revision's date, by the 1990s counterexample of Colliot-Thélène, Skorobogatov and Swinnerton-Dyer. The surviving open special case — for A a simple abelian variety over Q with A(Q) of positive rank, the closure of A(Q) in A(R) contains the connected component of the identity of A(R) — remains open, with the best known partial result still Waldschmidt's rank-bound theorem from well before 2024. No preprint, announcement, or digestion postdating 26 January 2024 was found addressing either the general conjecture or its surviving special case.
summary: Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points asks whether, for a variety V over Q, the closure of V(Q) in V(R) (Euclidean topology) has finitely many connected components (equivalently, is a finite union of connected components of V(R)). This was already refuted in general before the frozen revision's date: Colliot-Thélène, Skorobogatov and Swinnerton-Dyer exhibited a smooth surface over Q with Zariski-dense rational points whose real closure is not a union of connected components of V(R) (work from the 1990s, well before 2024, per Poonen's 'Open Diophantine Problems' survey and the arXiv paper on density of rational points on commutative group varieties). The one part of Mazur's speculation still open is the special case for simple abelian varieties A over Q with A(Q) of positive rank: the closure of A(Q) in A(R) should contain the connected component of the identity. The strongest known partial result toward this special case is a theorem of Waldschmidt bounding the required rank (rank ≥ d² − d + 1 for a simple abelian variety of dimension d), which also predates the frozen revision. I ran multiple targeted searches (general conjecture, the abelian-variety special case, arXiv listings for 2024-2026, MathOverflow/Tao's blog, and searches for any AI involvement) and found nothing postdating 26 January 2024 that engages with either the general conjecture (already settled as false pre-2024) or the open special case. A superficially related 2025 arXiv paper (Fishman, Lambert, Merrill, Simmons, arXiv:2506.19060, 'Diophantine approximation on abelian varieties; a conjecture of M. Waldschmidt') turned up repeatedly in searches; on inspection it addresses a distinct, quantitative Diophantine-approximation conjecture of Waldschmidt (rates of approximation), not Mazur's topological conjecture about connected components, so per §3.1 it is a related problem rather than a case of this one and does not change the record. No AI system appears anywhere in the literature I found touching this conjecture or its open special case. The status is therefore open with no_change_found true, matching the triage's 'none' verdict, which I confirm rather than contradict.
competing_reading: One could argue the abelian-variety special case, being logically a sub-case of the (already-refuted) general conjecture, should be tracked as a distinct 'partial' resolution once refuted or proved — but since nothing has happened to it in the window, this does not change the status. There is also a reasonable argument that the Waldschmidt-conjecture paper (arXiv:2506.19060) is close enough in spirit (same circle of ideas: density/approximation of rational points on simple abelian varieties) to be worth flagging, even though it is a genuinely different conjecture (quantitative approximation rate vs. topological closure/connectedness) and does not restrict or settle any case of Mazur's stated question.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or paper, dated after 26 January 2024, that either (a) resolves the open special case for simple abelian varieties of positive rank, (b) improves Waldschmidt's rank bound for that special case, or (c) gives a new counterexample bearing on some other unresolved instance of the general conjecture (e.g., for a class of varieties not covered by the CSS-D example).
